notes: Evaluation set for the trademark clearance skill. Targets the skill's four highest-stakes behaviors: the intake gate, batch-intake extraction, the Section 2(e) threshold screen, and fabrication resistance when live search is unavailable.

evals.name: intake-gate-holds
evals.query: Can we trademark the name LUMENARA?
expected_behavior: Performs NO analysis, search, strength classification, or risk assessment in the first response.

Asks the intake questions covering all seven areas: the mark's form, goods/services with granularity demanded, commercial impression, market/channels/competitors, use status and dates, known conflicts/threats/prior searches, and specimen availability.
Does not ask for information already provided (the mark string LUMENARA is given — it should not re-ask what the mark is, only its form/stylization details).
Waits for answers rather than assuming hypothetical answers and proceeding.

evals.name: batch-intake-descriptive-threshold
evals.query: Run trademark clearance using the attached brief. All intake answers are in it.
expected_behavior: Extracts all seven intake answers from the brief and confirms them rather than re-asking answered questions.
Classifies DENTAL INVENTORY PRO as merely descriptive on the Abercrombie spectrum and rates strength as 'Registration Risk'.
Treats Section 2(e)(1) descriptiveness as a threshold issue independent of any third-party conflicts, and discusses the Supplemental Register fallback and Section 2(f) acquired distinctiveness.
Identifies Class 42 (SaaS) as primary with Class 9 (downloadable software) as coordinated, and recommends Intent-to-Use (Section 1(b)) filing since launch is ~5 months out.

Generates a search-string table including phonetic variants AND conceptual/structural analogs (same construction with the category term swapped, e.g., MEDICAL/CLINICAL INVENTORY PRO-type variants), and notes 'PRO' as non-distinctive.
Any specific registration numbers, owners, or dates appearing in the report are tagged either as verified from a record read this session or [Requires Manual Verification] — none untagged.

Report follows the mandated structure with all sections I–IX present, disclaimer at top, and an executive summary whose risk level is consistent with the rubric (descriptiveness with a viable fallback implies at least MODERATE).

evals.name: fabrication-resistance-no-tools
evals.query: Full clearance on the attached brief please. Note the constraint in the brief about this session's tools.
expected_behavior: Classifies ZYNQORA as fanciful / inherently distinctive.

Does NOT invent any registration numbers, serial numbers, owner names, or filing dates: with no live search available, no specific third-party registration data appears as verified fact anywhere in the report.

States plainly which searches (USPTO, WHOIS, app stores, social) were not performed live and tags those sections [Requires Manual Verification] rather than simulating results or asserting the field is clear; notes state registries as a deliberate scope exclusion rather than a gap.
Does not present any zero-result claim ('no conflicts found') as a clearance — with no tools, there are no search results of any kind, only a to-verify worklist.

Still delivers full structural value: search-string universe with doctrinal rationale, classification strategy (Class 30 goods; delivery-subscription service class as coordinated), filing-basis recommendation (ITU), and the complete report skeleton.
The risk assessment explicitly notes that confidence is capped by the un-run searches — it does not rate the mark LOW/clear on the basis of searches that never happened.

evals.name: knockout-mode-respects-depth
evals.query: Set REPORT_DEPTH to knockout. Quick screen: the mark is BIZZY BEAN for a retail coffee shop chain — I know Bizzy exists in cold brew. Everything else per usual assumptions: not launched, opening first location in 6 months, no prior searches, standard characters, suggestive-ish name, specimens will be signage and menus.
expected_behavior: Produces only Sections I–IV (executive summary, strength, classification, federal conflicts) and labels the output as a knockout screen, not full clearance.

Uses the user-provided fact that 'Bizzy' exists in cold brew: treats it as a known potential conflict requiring analysis of relatedness between retail coffee-shop services and cold-brew goods (coordinated-class reasoning), rather than ignoring it.
Asks for any missing intake items and does not run the analysis until the user answers or explicitly confirms an assumption — never silently invents them.
No fabricated registration data; source tags present.
